history.dynasty: None (associated with the Sabarimala Ayyappa shrine tradition; idol installed by Thanthri Brahmasree Kandararu Maheswararu)
history.period: Medieval origin (mythological); prior to fire damage only a Peeda Prathishta (holy seat) existed here; present structure reconstructed within the last decade
history.summary: Sub-shrine of the Sabarimala complex located a few yards from the Sannidhanam, of near-equal importance to the Ayyappa shrine. Legend: Malikappurathamma, the divine daughter of Cheerappanchira Panicker of Muhamma (also named Subhadra, Poonkodi, Leela or Lalitha in some accounts), fell in love with Ayyappa while he learned Kalaripayattu from her family; he declined marriage on grounds of his vow of eternal celibacy but stipulated he would marry her if no Kanni Ayyappans (first-time pilgrims) ever arrived at Sabarimala. Another account says she was the demoness Mahishi, freed from sin after being slain by Ayyappa, who asked to marry him. The goddess holds a Sankh, Chakram and Varada Abhya Mudra; the idol is now covered with a gold golaka, and the conical roof and sopanam are gold-covered. During Makaravilakku, the Malikappurathamma ezhunnallathu procession carries her thidambu on a caparisoned elephant from Malikappuram toward the Pathinettampadi, concluding at Saramkuthi where Kanni Ayyappans stick arrows marking their arrival; on seeing them, she returns to her shrine.

name: Malikappurathu Amma Temple
town_description: Sabarimala is a pilgrim centre in the Western Ghats of Pathanamthitta district, Kerala, deep in the Periyar Tiger Reserve forest at about 468 metres elevation. It is home to one of the largest annual pilgrimages in the world, drawing 40-50 million devotees to the Ayyappa shrine each year. The Malikappuram shrine sits within the temple complex a short walk from the main Sannidhanam.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism; consort-tradition tied to Ayyappa worship)

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport ~175 km (verify); Cochin International Airport ~200 km (verify)
travel.railway: Chengannur railway station ~90 km (verify), then bus/taxi to Pamba
travel.road: Road goes to Pamba; from Pamba a ~5.5 km uphill trek (2-3 hours) reaches the Sannidhanam; Malikappuram temple is ~100 m from the main shrine

visitor_information.best_time: Mandalam-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season (November-January); temple also opens the first five days of each Malayalam month and on Vishu (verify)
visitor_information.opening_hours: During Mandalam season roughly 3 AM-11 PM; monthly openings roughly 6 AM-1 PM and 4:30 PM-7:30 PM — schedules vary and sources conflict (verify)
